# Data Source: stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer

A transfer of money out of a Treasury financial account to another financial account or a bank account the connected account owns. It lives on a connected account, so read it through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is that account. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "connected_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "The connected account the object lives on."
}

provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "connected"
  stripe_account = var.connected_account
}

data "stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer" "sweep" {
  provider = stripe.connected
  id       = "obt_1MtYCCLkdIwHu7ixGq6ws9GD"
}

output "outbound_transfer_status" {
  value = data.stripe_treasury_outbound_transfer.sweep.status
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the treasury outbound transfer to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) to be transferred.
* `cancelable` - Returns `true` if the object can be canceled, and `false` otherwise.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `destination_payment_method` - The PaymentMethod to use as the payment instrument for the OutboundTransfer.
* `destination_payment_method_data` - Hash used to generate the PaymentMethod to be used for this OutboundTransfer. Exclusive with `destination_payment_method`. See [`destination_payment_method_data`](#destination_payment_method_data) below.
* `destination_payment_method_details` - See [`destination_payment_method_details`](#destination_payment_method_details) below.
* `destination_payment_method_options` - Hash describing payment method configuration details. See [`destination_payment_method_options`](#destination_payment_method_options) below.
* `expected_arrival_date` - The date when funds are expected to arrive in the destination account.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount to pull funds from.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format. Individual keys can be unset by posting an empty value to them. All keys can be unset by posting an empty value to `metadata`.
* `returned_details` - Details about a returned OutboundTransfer. Only set when the status is `returned`. See [`returned_details`](#returned_details) below.
* `statement_descriptor` - Statement descriptor to be shown on the receiving end of an OutboundTransfer. Maximum 10 characters for `ach` transfers or 140 characters for `us_domestic_wire` transfers. The default value is "transfer". Can only include -#.$&*, spaces, and alphanumeric characters.
* `status` - Current status of the OutboundTransfer: `processing`, `failed`, `canceled`, `posted`, `returned`. An OutboundTransfer is `processing` if it has been created and is pending. The status changes to `posted` once the OutboundTransfer has been "confirmed" and funds have left the account, or to `failed` or `canceled`. If an OutboundTransfer fails to arrive at its destination, its status will change to `returned`. Possible values: `canceled`, `failed`, `posted`, `processing`, `returned`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`status_transitions`](#status_transitions) below.
* `tracking_details` - Details about network-specific tracking information if available. See [`tracking_details`](#tracking_details) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

### `destination_payment_method_data`

The `destination_payment_method_data` attribute supports:

* `financial_account` -
* `type` - Possible values: `financial_account`.

<a id="destination_payment_method_details"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details`

The `destination_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `billing_details` - See [`destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`](#destination_payment_method_details.billing_details) below.
* `financial_account` - See [`destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`](#destination_payment_method_details.financial_account) below.
* `type` - The type of the payment method used in the OutboundTransfer. Possible values: `financial_account`, `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="destination_payment_method_details.billing_details"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`

The `destination_payment_method_details.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`](#destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.

<a id="destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="destination_payment_method_details.financial_account"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`

The `destination_payment_method_details.financial_account` attribute supports:

* `id` - Token of the FinancialAccount.
* `network` - The rails used to send funds. Possible values: `stripe`.

<a id="destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `network` - The network rails used. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/money-movement/timelines) to learn more about money movement timelines for each network type. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.

<a id="destination_payment_method_options"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_options`

The `destination_payment_method_options` attribute supports:

* `us_bank_account` - See [`destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account`](#destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account"></a>
### `destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account`

The `destination_payment_method_options.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `network` - Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.

<a id="returned_details"></a>
### `returned_details`

The `returned_details` attribute supports:

* `code` - Reason for the return. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_ownership_changed`, `declined`, `incorrect_account_holder_name`, `invalid_account_number`, `invalid_currency`, `no_account`, `other`.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="status_transitions"></a>
### `status_transitions`

The `status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `canceled_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `canceled`
* `failed_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `failed`
* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `posted`
* `returned_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `returned`

<a id="tracking_details"></a>
### `tracking_details`

The `tracking_details` attribute supports:

* `ach` - See [`tracking_details.ach`](#tracking_details.ach) below.
* `type` - The US bank account network used to send funds. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `us_domestic_wire` - See [`tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`](#tracking_details.us_domestic_wire) below.

<a id="tracking_details.ach"></a>
### `tracking_details.ach`

The `tracking_details.ach` attribute supports:

* `trace_id` - ACH trace ID of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `ach` network.

<a id="tracking_details.us_domestic_wire"></a>
### `tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`

The `tracking_details.us_domestic_wire` attribute supports:

* `chips` - CHIPS System Sequence Number (SSN) of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `imad` - IMAD of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `omad` - OMAD of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
